H3808.d: not (the simple or abs. negation); by implication, no; often used with other particles

H3899.d: food (for man or beast), especially bread, or grain (for making it)

H3847.d: properly, wrap around, i.e. (by implication) to put on a garment or clothe (oneself, or another), literally or figuratively

H3858.d: a blaze; also (from the idea of enwrapping) magic (as covert)

H3820.d: the heart; also used (figuratively) very widely for the feelings, the will and even the intellect; likewise for the centre of anything

H3866.d: a Ludite or inhabitants of Lud (only in plural)

H3853.d: Lehabim, a son of Mizraim, and his descendants
fb: A people descended from Mizraim, the ancestor of Egypt, in the Table of Nations. The name is widely tied to the Lebu of Egyptian inscriptions, ancestors of the Libyans on the coast west of Egypt.

H3865.d: Lud, the name of two nations
fb: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
Shem's son. His people are usually taken to be the Lydians of Asia Minor. Some later passages may mean a people in Africa instead.

H3835.d: to be (or become) white; to make bricks

H3843.d: a brick (from the whiteness of the clay)

fb: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs

Abraham's nephew, who came with him from Ur. When their herdsmen started fighting and they split, Lot took the green Jordan valley and ended up living by Sodom. Angels dragged him out before it burned, and his wife looked back and became a pillar of salt. Afterwards his two daughters got him drunk and had sons by him, the fathers of Moab and Ammon.

H3863.d: a conditional particle; if; by implication (interj. as a wish) would that!

H3885.d: to stop (usually over night); by implication, to stay permanently; hence (in a bad sense) to be obstinate (especially in words, to complain)

H3811.d: to tire; (figuratively) to be (or make) disgusted

H3824.d: the heart (as the most interior organ);

H3837.d: Laban, a Mesopotamian; also a place in the Desert
fb: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs

Rebekah's brother and Jacob's uncle, and then his father-in-law twice, after he slipped Leah in where Rachel should have been and got fourteen years of work out of him. He kept changing Jacob's wages as the flocks grew. Jacob finally slipped away with his family, and the two parted under a covenant, not with a fight.
Named once, in Deuteronomy, and nowhere else.
The word means "peoples." It names a group of Arabian tribes from Dedan, Abraham's grandson through Keturah, listed with Asshurim and Letushim.

H3870.d: Luz, the name of two places in Palestine
fb: It was the old Canaanite name of Bethel, where Jacob dreamed of the stairway to heaven, and it hung on in a nearby town after Bethel was renamed.
Named once, in Judges, and nowhere else.
Woman living at the time of the Patriarchs

Jacob's first wife, given to him by her father Laban in place of Rachel, and Jacob only found out in the morning. He never loved her the way he loved Rachel. Genesis says God gave her children because she was unloved, and she bore six of the twelve sons, Judah among them.

H3867.d: properly, to twine, i.e. (by implication) to unite, to remain; also to borrow (as a form of obligation) or (caus.) to lend

fb: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs

Jacob's third son. He and Simeon massacred the men of Shechem after their sister Dinah was raped, and Jacob cursed them both for it on his deathbed. Even so, Levi's descendants became Israel's priestly tribe, given service at the tabernacle instead of land, partly for their zeal against the golden calf at Sinai.
Apostle living at the time of the New Testament
Mark and Luke name him twice, and he is a man from the New Testament.

H3839.d: some sort of whitish tree, perhaps the storax

H3869.d: some kind of nut-tree, perhaps the almond

fb: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
He was a Horite chief whose sister Timna made him Esau's brother-in-law, and his people were living in Edom's land before Edom.

H3887.d: properly, to make mouths at, i.e. to scoff; hence (from the effort to pronounce a foreign language) to interpret, or (generally) intercede

H3856.d: to be rabid (figuratively, insane); also (from the exhaustion of frenzy) to languish

H3833.d: a lion (properly, a lioness as the fiercer (although not a roarer;))

H3830.d: a garment (literally or figuratively); by implication (euphemistically) a wife

H3898.d: to feed on; figuratively, to consume; by implication, to battle (as destruction)

H3881.d: a Levite or descendant of Levi
fb: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
An old spelling of Levite, found in a few manuscripts and translations for the tribe of Levi.
Levite living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
Gershon's son, Levi's grandson, and the head of one of the Levitical clans.
Levite living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
1 Chronicles names him once, and he is a Levite from the wilderness years.

H3871.d: probably meaning to glisten; a tablet (as polished), of stone, wood or metal

H3802.d: the shoulder (proper, i.e. upper end of the arm; as being the spot where the garments hang); figuratively, side-piece or lateral projection of anything

H3828.d: frankincense (from its whiteness or perhaps that of its smoke)

H3849.d: a log or measure for liquids

H3846.d: a Libnite or descendants of Libni (collectively)
fb: Levite living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
Libni's clan, Levites from Gershon's line, who looked after the coverings and hangings of the tabernacle on the march.
Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
Eliasaph's father, named only to say whose son the leader of the Gershonite Levites in the wilderness was.

H3841.d: Libnah, a place in the Desert and one in Palestine
fb: A royal Canaanite city near Lachish that Joshua took and gave to the Levites in Judah. It held out against Sennacherib's Assyrians. Hamutal, Josiah's wife and mother of two of Judah's last kings, came from there.
Named twice, in Numbers, and nowhere else.

H3844.d: Lebanon, a mountain range in Palestine
fb: Two mountain ridges along the coast, Lebanon proper to the west and the Anti-Lebanon rising to Mount Hermon, with the Beqaa Valley between. Solomon's temple and palace were built of its cedar, cut and floated south under a deal with Hiram of Tyre. Israel was promised it and never took all of it.

H3895.d: the cheek (from its fleshiness); hence, the jaw-bone

H3857.d: properly, to lick, i.e. (by implication) to blaze

fb: A town where, in 2 Samuel 9, a lame son of the old royal house is found living in another man's home. Amos plays on its name, which sounds like "nothing."
"Lionesses." One of Judah's southernmost towns, by the Edom border, and probably the same as Beth-lebaoth, which went to Simeon.

H3851.d: a flash; figuratively, a sharply polished blade or point of a weapon

fb: "Jawbone." The Philistines gathered here to take Samson, and he broke his ropes and killed a thousand of them with a donkey's jawbone. Afterwards, parched, he called on God, and a spring opened in a hollow there.

H3803.d: to enclose; hence (in a friendly sense) to crown, (in a hostile one) to besiege; also to wait (as restraining oneself)

fb: Judges 21:19 uses it to say where Shiloh was, on the road between Bethel and Shechem, when the men of Benjamin grabbed wives from the girls dancing at the festival. It is generally identified with Lubban, south of Nablus, which still keeps the name.

H3823.d: properly, to be enclosed (as if with fat); by implication (as denominative from H3824 (לֵבָב)); to unheart; i.e. (in a good sense) transport (with love), or (in a bad sense) stultify; to make cakes

H3834.d: a cake (either as fried or turned)

fb: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
One of Jahath's sons, in Judah's line through Shobal. Nothing else is recorded of him.

They called it Lydda in New Testament Greek. Over seven hundred people came back from exile to this town of Benjamin, on the plain along the road from Jerusalem to Joppa. Modern Lod, by Tel Aviv's airport, keeps the name.

H3864.d: a Libyan or inhabitant of interior Africa (only in plural)

H3838.d: Lebana or Lebanah, one of the Nethinim
fb: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
Ancestor of a family of temple servants, the Nethinim, who came back from Babylon with Zerubbabel.
Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs

They belonged to the tribe of Levi and served at the tabernacle and later the temple, helping the priests, who came from Aaron's branch of the same tribe. Their work was religious, so they got no tribal land, only forty eight towns among the other tribes and the tithes of Israel. Over time they carried and guarded the holy things, sang, kept the gates, and taught the law.

H3804.d: properly, a circlet, i.e. a diadem

H3882.d: a wreathed animal, i.e. a serpent (especially the crocodile or some other large sea-monster); figuratively, the constellation of the dragon; also as a symbol of Babylon

H3886.d: to gulp; figuratively, to be rash

H3894.d: properly, eaten, i.e. food; also flesh, i.e. body

H3800.d: properly, something carved out, i.e. ore; hence, gold (pure as originally mined)

H3868.d: to turn aside , i.e. (literally) to depart, (figuratively) be perverse

H3859.d: properly, to burn in, i.e. (figuratively) to rankle

H3872.d: Luchith, a place East of the Jordan
fb: In Isaiah and Jeremiah, refugees climb the road up to Luhith in Moab weeping. It was somewhere between Zoar and Horonaim, exactly where is unknown.

H3819.d: Lo-Ruchamah, the symbolic name of a son of Hosea
fb: Woman living at the time of Divided Monarchy
"Not pitied." Hosea's daughter carried the name as a sign that God would stop showing mercy to the northern kingdom, and when Hosea 2:23 turns it to "loved," Paul hears in it the Gentiles brought in.

H3818.d: Lo-Ammi, the symbolic name of a son of Hosea
fb: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy

"Not my people." God told Hosea to give his second son by Gomer that name, to say Israel's northern kingdom was being cast off. Later in the book it is turned round, and those called "not my people" are to be called sons of the living God. Paul reads that reversal as the Gentiles coming in.
